about: The timeline as rows: one per signal, with who published it (publisher) where the source has a URL. Built by tools/graph-build.mjs from the incident's JSON; every row carries label, source, read and origin. Not a warning service.

rows.label: evidence

AEMET's post is timed 10:20:11 (read through Bluesky's public API). IPMA's communiqué no. 1 can no longer be read (its page and feed carry only no. 2), so whether 13:17 was its first publication or an edit is not established

rows.label: hypothesis
rows.text: analysis (incident.meteorologist@, hypothesis, confidence low to medium): the official and model data are consistent with the centre passing very close to Lisbon at about 17:00 to 18:00 Wednesday, more likely just south of it (met.no's pressure minimum 986.7 hPa at 17:00 to 18:00 and a 160° wind swing in an hour; the guidance has moved). Against: IPMA's red wind unchanged, its track text already includes Lisbon, no communiqué no. 3, point models move. It does not lower the danger: the worst moves toward the passage, about 16:00 to 19:00, and a lull near the centre is not the end. Wednesday tests it: wind backing east then north and pressure near 987 hPa means it passed south
rows.via: storm-charles.promptugal.news; data/weather/analysis.md section 7 (d6e8aace1); address:  (internal analysis; read 02:15, by incident.researcher@)

rows.label: fact
rows.text: The alert situation's legal text, read at source: Despacho n.º 13773-A/2026 (Diário da República n.º 218/2026, Suplemento, Série II, 10 November), by the Presidency of the Council of Ministers and nine ministries, under Lei 27/2006: in force 00:00 to 23:59 on 11 November, measures 2(a) to (e) and readiness measures 3(a) to (f). It suspends outdoor events (2(b)) and does not mention Web Summit: "formally advised" has no legal text; it remains the organisers' own wording (their page, 19:09) beside the government's recommendation reported at 17:53
rows.via: Diário da República, Despacho 13773-A/2026; read 02:28 by incident.researcher@ (the site is a JavaScript app; read with a browser)

rows.label: hypothesis
rows.text: analysis (incident.meteorologist@, hypothesis, re-weighed; supersedes the 00:00 reading): which side of Lisbon the centre passes is unsettled: "just south of Lisbon" drops to low confidence (was medium), because met.no's 01:19 run veers the wind through south to west with its strongest mean wind (56 to 58 km/h) at 14:00 to 15:00 and lowest pressure 987.7 hPa at 15:00, the pattern of a centre passing just north; IPMA's hourly model (an older run) and its forecasters on radio lean the other way. What holds across the inputs (medium confidence): the centre passes very close to Lisbon between about 15:00 and 18:00. The press headline "less wind for Lisbon" is not supported by these inputs. IPMA's red warnings for Lisbon stand; this is our analysis, not a forecast
rows.via: data/weather/analysis.md section 7b (7 and 7a kept, dated); met.no and IPMA figures in data/weather/forecast.json, read 01:19 and 02:22

rows.label: evidence
rows.text: Madeira: 71 occurrences between 20:00 on Tuesday and 02:00 on Wednesday (22 floodings, 13 landslides, 7 fallen trees; Machico 20, Santa Cruz 18, Funchal and Câmara de Lobos 10 each, Porto Santo 1), reported by DN Madeira (published 02:10) as the regional civil protection's count. That count reaches the press through the service's platform for the media, which is not public; its own site carries no count (read 03:51). No notice from Porto Santo's municipality or the ports authority on the measures a mayor is reported to have confirmed: not established

Observed: the highest mean wind at an IPMA station is 93.2 km/h at Areeiro (the hour labelled 02:00; the stations report no gusts); the highest measured gust is still the airport's 98 km/h at 02:30 (s-1111T0238)

rows.label: hypothesis
rows.text: analysis (incident.meteorologist@, hypothesis; supersedes the reading of 02:29): IPMA's new hourly model run (07:56) now shows the same pattern as MET Norway's: wind from the east around midday, a lull of about 11 km/h at 13:00, then south 40 km/h at 14:00 and south-west 35 km/h at 15:00, turning west and north-west; MET Norway (09:19) has its strongest mean wind, 55 km/h, and its lowest pressure, 988.8 hPa, at 15:00. Reading: the centre passes close to Lisbon and just north of it between about 13:00 and 15:00 (which side: medium confidence); the strongest wind most likely between 14:00 and 16:00; the lull around 12:00 to 13:00 is not the end. IPMA's warnings are what stand: red rain to 18:00, orange wind to 21:00. Observed at Lisbon airport at 09:00: south-south-east 20 km/h with rain and mist, visibility 3 km, no gust above the warned level; IPMA's stations show 2 to 8 mm of rain an hour and rising. This is our analysis, not a forecast

rows.label: hypothesis
rows.text: analysis (incident.meteorologist@, hypothesis) on the press's "two centres" (s-1111T0939). Facts: IPMA has published nothing in writing about two centres (no communiqué after no. 2, which speaks of one; its CAP texts do not describe the low). Madeira airport's pressure was lowest at 991 hPa at 06:30, its wind swung from south-west to north-east between 07:00 and 08:00, and its pressure is rising again (997 hPa); Lisbon airport's pressure has fallen steadily from 1005 hPa at 04:00 to 1000 hPa at 09:30. Reading (medium confidence): one centre cannot have passed Madeira at 06:30 to 08:00 and reach Lisbon at 13:00 to 15:00, 966 km away, without moving at 140 to 160 km/h, so Madeira's swing was most likely a separate feature: consistent with two centres, not proof of them. The reading of 09:22 stands: a centre close to and just north of Lisbon about 13:00 to 15:00, the strongest wind most likely 14:00 to 16:00. The test: Lisbon's pressure bottoming near 988 to 992 hPa about 14:00 to 15:00, with the wind veering through south-west. Our analysis, not a forecast

Fact: read from IPMA's own file; it matches the CAP batch (s-1111T1234)

rows.label: fact
rows.text: IPMA shortens Lisbon's warnings (CAP batch sent 12:33:13, nine messages; seen in MeteoAlarm's feed at 12:46): Lisboa: red rain 12:34 to 15:00 (was to 18:00), then yellow rain 15:00 to 18:00; orange wind 12:34 to 18:00 (was to 21:00), its text now «Rajadas até 90 km/h, podendo atingir 110 km/h nos locais mais expostos» (the 07:16 message said gusts up to 120 km/h); no message for the sea, whose orange 12:00 to 21:00 and yellow 21:00 to 03:00 stand. Setúbal: the same for rain, orange wind to 18:00. Beja orange wind 12:34 to 18:00; Santarém and Leiria yellow wind 12:34 to 18:00. Fact: read from IPMA's CAP messages, and IPMA's own warnings page shows the same at 13:25 («Última atualização: […] 12:33»; Lisboa still labelled «Vermelho»; captured by incident.archivist@); IPMA's open-data file still lagged at 13:22

rows.label: evidence
rows.text: Público (article 12:00, updated 12:17; post 12:28) titles «Web Summit […] já confirmou o regresso amanhã» and captions «Meo Arena […] e os pavilhões da FIL […] reabrem quinta-feira, confirma a organização da Web Summit»; it does not say where or when the organisers confirmed it, and the rest is behind its paywall. Evidence: the press, not the organisers. The organisers' own accounts have posted nothing since 10 Nov 17:36 (read 12:46 by incident.social@); their 19:09 update said Day 3 «aims to proceed as planned» (the headline). Lusa at 11:59, citing ANA: 360 flights cancelled at Portuguese airports (evidence; s-1111T1236 had 334 from ECO)
rows.via: Público article and Bluesky post, read 12:52 by incident.conductor@ (offered by incident.social@ 12:52); Lusa's Bluesky post 11:59

rows.label: fact
rows.text: Lusoponte's own notice («Atualização: 11 de novembro, 11h30», Lisbon time = UTC): since 11:30, a maximum of 60 km/h on the 25 de Abril and 80 km/h on the Vasco da Gama, «devido à intensificação da chuva e à visibilidade reduzida»; for motorcycles, soft-top and other wind-prone vehicles crossing «continua a ser desaconselhada»; it may change «a qualquer momento». Fact: read at the bridges' operator; it confirms what s-1111T1236 had from the press. Also on its site: its Viacard shops closed on 11 November for the weather (notice dated 10 November)
rows.via: lusoponte.pt notice «Velocidade reduzida nas pontes 25 de Abril e Vasco da Gama», read 12:49 by incident.transport@ (not reachable from the conductor's machine at 12:54)

rows.label: evidence
rows.text: Thursday reported confirmed. 24 Notícias: Web Summit «vai reabrir portas esta quinta-feira, 12 de novembro, para o último dia da edição de 2026, confirmou a organização numa comunicação enviada aos participantes esta quarta-feira»; «a quinta-feira mais movimentada de sempre da Web Summit»; part of Wednesday's programme moved to Thursday. PrompTugal's social.watch desk reports a Web Summit blog post titled «Announcement» at 12:04 (from the blog's index; not read here). Evidence: the press relaying the organisers' message (with Público, s-1111T1252); not read at the organisers' own page, which is on hold here (its terms forbid automated reading)
rows.via: 24 Notícias, read 13:04 by incident.conductor@; PrompTugal social.watch signals (899abcf), read 13:04

rows.label: fact
rows.text: Lisbon at 13:00: the airport observed east 20 km/h (no gust reported), heavy rain, visibility 1.5 km, 991 hPa, the pressure down 8 hPa since 10:00 and still falling. In the hour labelled 12:00: Relógio 18.7 mm, Geofísico 18.1; Relógio 57.7 mm in six hours (07:00 to 12:00), the largest six-hour total at IPMA's Lisbon stations in the warning window (the storm's largest single hour is still Barreiro, 18.9 mm, 10 Nov 01:00). No new CAP for Lisbon since 12:33:13; IPMA's open-data file still shows the older windows. Hypothesis (incident.meteorology@, analysis 20): the centre has not yet passed (east wind, falling pressure), its closest approach more likely 14:00 to 16:00; IPMA's messages expect the rain to ease from 15:00
rows.via: METAR LPPT 1300Z; IPMA hourly station observations; IPMA CAP via MeteoAlarm; read 13:22 by incident.meteorology@
